key_insight: Ranking-PE changes prompt optimization from accuracy-based scoring to pairwise ranking, so the search objective directly matches AUROC for imbalanced clinical diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This matters because clinical datasets are often highly imbalanced, and a model that looks accurate can still fail to identify the higher-risk cases that matter most.
method: Replace per-example correctness with pairwise positive-vs-negative ordering in the prompt-evolution score matrix.
Use the resulting column average as empirical AUROC via the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney identity.
Apply the same ranking-based swap in dominance checks, reflection feedback, and final candidate selection without extra model calls.
evidence_signal: Across three MIMIC diseases, ranking-aware prompt evolution improved AUROC by +5.8 points on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 points on MedGemma-4B versus accuracy-based prompt evolution.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a strong medical visual backbone, so prompt search alone cannot compensate for weak multimodal pretraining or vision tuning.
paper_title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
